items.headline: "We view AI as a sliding scale. There will always be a human in the loop": Why Side signed an MOU with modl.ai to use AI for QA
items.excerpt: QA and localisation giant Side has signed a memorandum of understanding with modl.ai to fold automated AI agents into its game testing pipeline. Both companies argue AI bots can sweep repetitive regression passes while human testers stay responsible for judgement calls.

items.headline: Arm explains its mobile-first AI-reconstruction tech, a different tack from the "black box" approach of DLSS 5
items.excerpt: Arm details a neural upscaling and frame-reconstruction stack built for mobile GPUs, positioning it against Nvidia's DLSS 5. "Our networks are not generative, so they're not of the same nature as the latest DLSS model," the company says.

items.headline: European game developers fear AI will pressure them to work faster more than they fear losing their jobs
items.excerpt: A European games employment survey finds half of respondents worried AI will erode work quality, ahead of job-loss fears. 46% also say AI output makes it harder to assess a candidate's actual skills when hiring.

items.headline: "Hopefully a meteor will strike the earth soon": Game devs talk genAI witchhunts and visual literacy
items.excerpt: Developers at Failbetter, New Blood and other studios describe being wrongly accused of using generative AI by players hunting for tells. They argue sharpening visual and technical literacy is the only durable defence for hand-made art.

items.headline: It's still possible to make good Skyrim mods "without any use of AI" in 2026, says the maker of a DLC-sized Black Marsh expansion
items.excerpt: King of the Murkmire, a DLC-scale Skyrim expansion set in Black Marsh, shipped with its author stressing that no AI was used in its assets or writing. The release lands as AI voice and texture tools spread through the Bethesda modding scene.

items.headline: NBA 2K27 gives DLSS 5 a more faithful-looking debut than feared — if you own the LeBron of GPUs
items.excerpt: DLSS 5's generative neural rendering makes its first shipping-game appearance in NBA 2K27, and it is far subtler than Nvidia's demos suggested. The cost is severe: the filter remains a heavy performance brute even on top-end cards.

items.headline: After AI slop accusations, Humankind 2's studio proves its trailer was made by humans (and at least five chickens)
items.excerpt: Fans accused the new Humankind 2 trailer of being AI-generated, prompting the studio to publish its production breakdown. The team says traditional CG artists, a live-action crew and real animals made the spot.

items.headline: Saber Interactive won't change its comms strategy despite backlash over its AI writer controversy
items.excerpt: CCO Tim Willits says Saber is not adjusting how it communicates after its CEO's dispute over replacing a writer with AI. The studio maintains its position while the row over AI in narrative work continues.

items.headline: "This is super, super heavy": experts test Nvidia's graphics-altering DLSS 5 and find it really does tank frame rates
items.excerpt: Independent benchmarking of DLSS 5's neural rendering shows a steep frame-rate cost in its first shipping title. The findings sharpen the question of whether generative post-processing is worth the GPU budget.

items.headline: 'There is absolutely no generative AI in Space Marine 3', promises a Saber Interactive executive
items.excerpt: Saber publicly commits that no generative AI content ships in Space Marine 3, following weeks of scrutiny over the studio's AI stance. The pledge is now a marketing position as much as a production one.

items.headline: Saber CCO Tim Willits is still bullish on AI, but worried about its environmental cost
items.excerpt: Willits defends AI as a production accelerator while flagging the energy and water footprint of the data centres behind it. He points to orbital server proposals as a speculative fix.

items.headline: A new ReShade addon offloads DLSS 5 neural rendering to a second GPU, slashing the AI filter's performance hit
items.excerpt: Modders have built a ReShade addon that runs DLSS 5's neural rendering pass on a secondary graphics card. The workaround recovers most of the frame-rate lost to Nvidia's generative filter.

items.headline: Video game companies keep trying to bait and switch us with AI, and it sucks
items.excerpt: 1666: Amsterdam, Blood of the Dawnwalker and others insist AI assets never reached the shipped build — a claim that quietly ignores AI used earlier in production. Aftermath argues 'no AI in the final game' has become a rhetorical dodge.

items.headline: ArtStation has new owners who say they'll 'put artists first' by protecting work from AI scrapers
items.excerpt: ArtStation's new ownership says protection against AI training will become the platform default rather than an opt-in toggle. The portfolio site is the primary shop window for most working game artists.

items.headline: Report: EA's NHL 27 is using genAI for commentator voiceover, claims a sports broadcaster
items.excerpt: Veteran commentator John Buccigross says EA demonstrated a system that clones his voice to generate in-game commentary lines. It would be one of the highest-profile uses of synthetic voice in a major sports franchise.

items.headline: After the Stellar Blade: Blood Rain AI backlash, Shift Up's lead says concerns are taken "seriously" — but AI still has "a lot of influence" on development
items.excerpt: Shift Up responds to criticism of an AI-generated music video promoting Stellar Blade: Blood Rain. The studio head says player concerns are heard, while maintaining AI is now materially shaping how the game is built.
